coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, so none of the app's risky logic — client filtering/pagination, table sorting, the in-memory API cache, or species mapping — is covered by anything the team owns.

app/src/lib/format.ts:9-45 — pure helpers that would be the natural target for behavioural (input/output) tests, untouched
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: With zero tests written there is nothing to classify; the criterion defaults to the floor.

evidence: app/src — no low-value tests because there are no tests
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also no signal; per the rubric this scores 3.

findings.issue: No test script, no test runner, and zero test files in app/; the acceptance suite in tests/ is the only safety net.
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight runner (vitest or node:test) and start with unit tests for the pure helpers in src/lib/format.ts, the cards.ts mapping, and the MovesSection comparators — all trivially testable with no mocking.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled promise cache with 30s TTL negatively caches 404s (NotFoundError stored as the entry's value), so a resource requested before it exists stays 'Not found' for up to 30 seconds; also untested for eviction/dedup regressions.
findings.suggestion: Exclude 404 responses from the cache (or use a much shorter negative TTL), and add tests for hit/miss/expiry/404 behavior against a stubbed fetch.

findings.issue: Client-side filtering, pagination clamping, and URL-state sync (debounce effect with no dependency array, lastWritten ref reconciliation, toQuery default-omission) are the app's most intricate logic and are completely untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract readFilters/toQuery and the match/page-computation into pure functions and unit-test the edge cases: empty q, page beyond pageCount, page=abc, combined filters, default-param omission.

findings.issue: Sort comparators (missing-values-last in both directions, ascending-then-flip toggle, aria-sort placement) and the method-order rule (level-up, machine, egg, tutor, then alphabetical) have no regression protection.
findings.suggestion: Extract compareValues/compareMethods and the sort transform as pure functions and test them, including the descending-missing-last case the acceptance tests only sample lightly.

findings.issue: Pokémon→species mapping, alternate-form exclusion (id > MAX_SPECIES_ID), dedupe, and dex ordering are untested; a boundary or dedupe bug silently drops cards from Learned-by/ability/type lists.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test cardsFor with refs containing alternate-form IDs (>10000), duplicates, and unknown species ids, using a stubbed getSpeciesNames.

findings.issue: Data assembly for stats total, ability ordering/hidden markers, artwork fallback chain, and version-group ordering (default = highest order) is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for getMoves and the stat/ability derivations with representative API fixtures (e.g. Mr. Mime, Eevee, a Pokémon with hidden ability and null artwork).

findings.issue: No error boundary anywhere in the route tree; api.ts:35-36 throws a generic Error on non-404 API failures, which crashes the whole page render as an unhandled 500.
findings.suggestion: Add app/error.tsx (and route-level ones if useful) with a retry affordance, and add one test that a 500 from the API renders a friendly error page instead of a framework crash.

findings.issue: Pure, dependency-free helpers (humanize, dexNumber, latestEnglishFlavorText, cleanText, orMissing, idFromUrl) encode spec-critical rules but have no tests despite being the cheapest code in the repo to test.
findings.suggestion: A dozen table-driven unit cases here would pin the display rules (em dash, whitespace collapse, latest-English selection) permanently.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — leaving the harness-owned acceptance suite as the only guard over genuinely intricate logic: debounced URL-state filtering, multi-column sorting with missing-values-last semantics, and a hand-rolled API cache that negatively caches 404s for 30s. The pure helpers in lib/format.ts and lib/cards.ts would have been nearly free to test and would have caught most future regressions. As it stands, any refactor of the data or filter layer ships blind.
